newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot electricity prices steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot electricity prices steady to lower.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) were steady to lower Thursday, although traders said they did expect some price increases with forecast cold weather over the weekend.

Temperatures through much of Texas were forecast to be 15 to 30 degrees below normal through early next week, while longer term predictions called for below normal tempertures in north Texas and near normal temperatures in south Texas from January 19 to 23.
"With this cold front coming in we should see prices start to move up (Friday)," said on ERCOT marketer.
Weaker natural gas prices put immediate downward pressure on ERCOT electricity prices however.
ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Friday delivery was talked lower in the $34.50-36.50 range from $35.00-39.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) on Wednesday, brokers and marketers said.
ERCOT electricity for non-firm delivery during Thursday's heavy load hours was notationally assessed steady at $33.00-37.00 per MWh, the sources said.

Firm off-peak ERCOT deliveries for Friday delivery were valued steady to lower at $19.00-22.00 from $20.00-22.00 on Wednesday, while non-firm delivery during Friday's light load hours was notionally pegged steady at $17.00-19.00 per MWh.
February ERCOT power was valued slightly higher at $33.00-34.00 from $32.50-33.50 on Wednesday, the sources said.

Separately, Texas Utilities said Thursday its 1,150 megawatt Comanche Peak nuclear power unit 2 should reach 100 percent production by Friday morning following a weekend shutdown to repair a main feedwater valve.
